title: TrustLLM Benchmark Results at Sub-7B Scale
original_idea: Run the TrustLLM evaluation suite on small models (Phi-3-mini, Gemma-2B, Llama-3.2-1B). Compare dimension-by-dimension (truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness) against published 7B baselines.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Relevant for edge deployment safety but primarily a replication at smaller scale. Impact depends on whether meaningful differences are found.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: TrustLLM suite is open source, small models fit on consumer hardware. Straightforward to run and compare. Good beginner project.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Run existing benchmark on 3 small models, compare against published baselines. Clear, contained scope.

novelty.reasoning: TrustLLM (ICML 2024) evaluated 16 mainstream LLMs but primarily at 7B+ scale. The leaderboard and TrustGen/TrustEval toolkit (2025) expanded coverage. Small models like Phi-3-mini, Gemma-2B, and Llama-3.2-1B have been evaluated on capability benchmarks but a systematic TrustLLM dimension-by-dimension comparison at sub-7B scale against published 7B baselines has not been published. The general trustworthiness findings (e.g., over-alignment in Llama2-7b) are known, but sub-7B coverage is a gap.

citation_verification.note: TrustLLM is an ICML 2024 benchmark evaluating trustworthiness across truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, and machine ethics.
Microsoft's Phi-3-mini is a well-known small language model.
Google's Gemma-2B is a publicly available small model.
Meta's Llama-3.2-1B is a publicly available small model.
